verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              उक्तं त्वया बुद्धिमता यन्नान्यो वक्तुमर्हति। संशयानां हि निर्मोक्ता त्वन्नान्यो विद्यते भुवि॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said Intelligent as you are, you have said what none else is capable of saying. There is none else in the world but you who can settle all doubts.

verses.sanskrit: गृहे गृहे हि राजानः स्वस्य स्वस्य प्रियङ्कराः। न च साम्राज्यमाप्तास्ते सम्राट्शब्दो हि कृच्छ्रभाक्॥ २॥
verses.english: There are kings in every province engaged in doing good to their respective selves. But none of them has been able to become an Emperor. The title of Emperor is difficult to be achieved.

verses.sanskrit: कथं परानुभावज्ञः स्वं प्रशंसितुमर्हति। परेण समवेतस्तु यः प्रशस्यः स पूज्यते॥३॥
verses.english: He who knows the velour and the strength of others never applauds himself. He is really worthy of praise who even in fighting with his enemies bear himself with all commendation.

verses.sanskrit: विशाला बहुला भूमिर्बहुरत्नसमाचिता। दूरं गत्वा विजानाति श्रेयो वृष्णिकुलोद्वह॥ ४॥
verses.english: O supporter of the Vrishni dignity, man's desires and propensities are varied and extensive like the wide earth adorned with various gems and jewels. As by travelling in distant places experiences is gained, so man can get the highest good by the highest culture of his understanding.

verses.sanskrit: शममेव परं मन्ये शमात्क्षेमं भवेन्मम। आरम्भे पारमेष्ठ्यं तु न प्राप्यमिति मे मतिः॥ ५॥
verses.english: I consider peace of mind as the highest quality, for from peace of mind proceeds prosperity. In my opinion, if I undertake to perform this sacrifice, I shall not win the highest reward.

verses.sanskrit: एवमेते हि जानन्ति कुले जाता मनस्विनः। कश्चित्कदाचिदेतेषां भवेच्छ्रेष्ठो जनार्दन॥६॥
verses.english: O Janardana, these intelligent and powerful men born in our race think that one amongst them will at one time become the foremost man amongst all the Kshatriyas.

verses.sanskrit: वयं यैव महाभाग जरासन्धभयात्तदा। शङ्किताः स्म महाभाग द्वौरात्म्यात्तस्य चानघ॥ ७॥
verses.english: But, O exalted one, O sinless being, we also were all alarmed at the prowess and the wickedness of the king Jarasandha, O hero, invincible in battle, O lord, the prowess of your arms in our refuge. When you are alarıned at Jarasandha's might, how should I consider my self strong (enough to cope with him)?
verses.bhavadeepa: कृष्णमेवोद्दिश्याह एवमिति । एते अस्मदीयाः सभासदः मनस्विनो भीमादयः श्रेष्ठः सर्वान् जेतुं समर्थो भविष्यतीति जानन्ति ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: अहं हि तव दुर्द्धर्ष भुजवीर्याश्रयः प्रभो। नात्मानं बलिनं मन्ये त्वयि तस्माद्विशङ्किते॥ ८॥
त्वत्सकाशाच्च रामाच्च भीमसेनाच्च माधव। अर्जुनाद्वा महाबाहो हन्तुं शक्यो न वेति वै। एवं जानन्हि वार्ष्णेय विमृशामि पुनः पुनः॥९॥
verses.english: O Madhava, O descendant of the Vrishni race, I have often become dispersed at the thought whether Jarasandha is at all capable of being killed by you, by Rama, or by Arjuna. O Keshava, what shall I say? You are my highest authority in everything. Having heard this, the able speaker Bhima then spoke these words:

verses.sanskrit: त्वं मे प्रमाणभूतोऽसि सर्वकार्येषु केशव। तच्छ्रुत्वा चाब्रवीद्भीमो वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥१०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: तथापि त्वत्प्रभृतीनां चतुर्णां मध्ये कश्चिदेनं हन्तुं समर्थोऽस्ति न वेति विमृशामि युष्माकमप्यनन्तशक्तित्वं जानान्नित्याह त्वत्सकाशादिति ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: अनारम्भपरो राजा वल्मीक इव सीदति। दुर्बलश्चानुपायेन बलिनं योऽधितिष्ठति॥११॥
verses.english: Bhima said The king, who is without any exertion, or the king who being himself weak and without resources, enter into hostility with one who is strong, perishes like an anthill.

verses.sanskrit: अतन्द्रितश्च प्रायेण दुर्बलो बलिनं रिपुम्। जयेत्सम्यक्प्रयोगेण नीत्याऽर्थानात्मनो हितान्॥ १२॥
verses.english: It is often seen that even weak king may defeat a strong enemy; and he may be come successful in his attempts by his wakefulness and by using policy.

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णेन यो मयि बलं जयः पार्थे धनञ्जये। मागधं साधयिष्याम इष्टिं त्रय इवाग्नयः॥
verses.english: (We have) in Krishna policy, in me strength, and in Partha (Dhananjaya) victory. Like the three (sacrificial) fires, we shall bring about the death of the king of Magadha (Jarasandha)

verses.sanskrit:
कृष्ण उवाच।
              अर्थानारभते बालो नानुबन्धमवेक्षते। तस्मादरिं न मृष्यन्ति बालमर्थपरायणम्॥१४॥
verses.english: Krishna said Men of immature understanding begin an act without having an eye to what may happen in future. It is, therefore, not a self-seeking enemy with immature understanding is ever forgiven by a sensible man.

verses.sanskrit: जित्वा जय्यान्यौवनाश्विः पालनाच्च भगीरथः। कार्तवीर्यस्तपोवीर्याद्बलात्तु भरतो विभुः॥ १५॥
verses.english: It has been heard by us that in the Satya Yuga, Yuvanashva brought every one under his sway, by the remission of taxes, Bhagiratha by kind treatment of his subjects, Kartavirya by his great asceticism, the lord Bharata by his extra ordinary prowess and Maruta by his prosperity, and thus they became emperors. O Yudhishthira, you who wish to acquire the imperial dignity, have the above mentioned) five qualities.
verses.bhavadeepa: भीमं प्रकोपयन्कृष्ण उवाच अर्थानिति । बालः अव्युत्पन्नः अनुबन्धं विपाकम् अर्थपरायणं स्वकार्यतत्परं न मृष्यन्ति न विचारयन्ति ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: ऋद्ध्या मरुत्तस्तान्पञ्च सम्राजस्त्वनुशुश्रुम। साम्राज्यमिच्छतस्ते तु सर्वाकारं युधिष्ठिर॥१६॥
निग्राह्यलक्षणं प्राप्तिर्धर्मार्थनयलक्षणैः॥ १७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: सर्वाकारं जयादिपञ्चप्रकारम् । यौवनाश्विप्रभृतयः एकैकेन गुणेन साम्राज्यं प्राप्तास्त्वं तु तत्सर्वैरपि गुणैरिच्छसीति भावः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: बार्हद्रथो जरासन्धस्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ। न चैनमनुरुद्ध्यन्ते कुलान्येकशतं नृपाः॥ १८॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, the son of Brihadratha, Jarasandha, is (also) one such (a candidate for the imperial dignity). One hundred families of kings have failed to oppose him.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादिह बलादेव साम्राज्यं कुरुते हि सः॥१९॥
रत्नभाजो हि राजानो जरासन्धमुपासते। न च तुष्यति तेनापि बाल्यादनयमास्थितः॥ २०॥
verses.english: He is ruling over an empire by his own great prowess. The monarchs that wear jewels wait upon and worship Jarasandha. Wicked from his childhood, he is not satisfied even such worship.

verses.sanskrit: मूर्धाभिषिक्तं नृपतिं प्रधानपुरुषो बलात्। आदत्ते न च नो दृष्टो भागः पुरुषतः क्वचित्॥२१॥
verses.english: Having become the foremost of all be attacks with force the kings that wear crowns. There is not to be found a single king who does not pay tributes to him.

verses.sanskrit: एवं सर्वान्वशे चक्रे जरासन्धः शतावरान्। तं दुर्बलतरो राजा कथं पार्थ उपैष्यति॥२२॥
verses.english: O son of Pritha, thus has be brought under his sway one hundred kings. How can then a weak king approach him with hostile intentions?
verses.bhavadeepa: नः अस्माभिर्न च दृष्टः जरासंधेन अभागः अस्वीकृतः पुरुषतः मूर्धाभिषिक्तेषु पुरुषेषु तेन सर्वे वशीकृता इत्यर्थः ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रोक्षितानां प्रमृष्टानां राज्ञां पशुपतेर्गृहे। पशूनामिव का प्रीतिर्जीविते भरतर्षभ॥२३॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, kept as they are prisoners in the temple of Shiva like so many animals to be offered to the sacrifice, do not these kings feel the greatest possible misery?

verses.sanskrit: क्षत्रियः शस्त्रमरणो यदा भवति सत्कृतः। ततः स्म मागधं सङ्ख्ये प्रतिबाधेम यद्वयम्॥ २४॥
verses.english: A Kshatriya who is killed by weapons (on the field of battle) is ever considered to be blessed. Why shall we not then assemble together and oppose the king of Magadha?

verses.sanskrit: षडशीतिः समानीताः शेषा राजंश्चतुर्दश। जरासन्धेन राजानस्ततः क्रूरं प्रवर्त्स्यते॥२५॥
verses.english: He has already brought under his sway eighty-six kings, only fourteen (more) are wanted to make the number of one hundred complete. As soon as he will collect them (the fourteen others), he will begin his cruel act(sacrificing them before Shiva).

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्नुयात्स यशो दीप्तं तत्र यो विघ्नमाचरेत्। जयेद्यश्च जरासन्धं स सम्राण्नियतं भवेत्॥ २६॥
verses.english: He, who will be able to prevent him from doing this act, will surely earn blazing fame. He, who will defeat Jarasandha, will certainly become the emperor of all the world.
verses.bhavadeepa: क्रूरं राजवधाख्यं कर्म । पशुपतये बलिदानं प्रवर्त्स्यते कारयिष्यति ॥२५॥
